voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The ship fired a rocket. No one answered. The Flannan Isles lighthouse, in Scotland's Outer Hebrides. Boxing Day, nineteen hundred.
The relief keeper, Joseph Moore, went ashore alone. He found the entrance gate closed. The outer door, closed.
Inside, he wrote, the fire was not lighted for some days. The beds were empty, just as they left them in the early morning.
He did not search further. He wrote that he knew only too well something serious had occurred.
That night, Moore and three men from the ship lit the light again. James Ducat, Thomas Marshall and Donald McArthur were never found.
